evidence: Clear module separation by domain (sources, processors, sessions, url, etc.) with well-defined responsibilities
Packages are organized into logical modules (dirhunt/sources, dirhunt/processors, dirhunt/tests) indicating high cohesion and low coupling
Heavy internal imports between modules (e.g., crawler.py imports processors, sessions, sources, etc.) without explicit service boundaries
Single executable entry point (dirhunt/cli.py → dirhunt/management.py → main) typical of monolithic tools
No evidence of network communication, RPC, or inter-process communication — all components run in-process
Shared data structures (Url, Sessions, Pool) used across modules indicate tight integration
Test suite organized per module, not per service, supporting monolithic structure
risks: Risk of tight coupling over time due to cross-module dependencies (e.g., Crawler imports many modules directly)
Testing may become slower as test suite grows (all tests in same process space)
